claims.text: Functional decline in older adults is typically recognized only after falls or observable gait impairment.
claims.poster_quote: Functional decline in older adults is typically recognized only after falls or observable gait impairment, closing the window for prevention.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Functional decline in older adults is typically recognized only after falls or observable gait impairment, closing the window for prevention.
claims.reason: Source: Abstract, first sentence. The claim matches the paper's statement directly.

claims.text: Routine biomarkers may hold early warning signals for functional decline.
claims.poster_quote: Routine biomarkers — already recorded but rarely analyzed longitudinally — may hold early warning signals.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We investigated whether temporal trajectories of routine biomarkers — already recorded but rarely analyzed longitudinally — can identify patients in the pre-clinical phase of mobility decline.
claims.reason: Source: Abstract, second sentence. The paper explicitly states that routine biomarkers may hold early warning signals for functional decline.

claims.text: Temporal trajectories of 12 routine biomarkers can identify patients in the preclinical phase of mobility decline.
claims.poster_quote: This study investigates whether temporal trajectories of 12 routine biomarkers can identify patients in the preclinical phase of mobility decline, using the All of Us Research Program (N=297,861; 11.1% cases).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Using the All of Us Research Program (N = 297,861; 11.1% cases), we derived trajectory features (slope, variability, delta, mean) for twelve biomarkers over a three-year pre-index window.
claims.reason: Source: Abstract, third sentence. The paper confirms the use of temporal trajectories of 12 biomarkers to identify patients in the preclinical phase of mobility decline.

claims.text: The All of Us Research Program dataset includes 297,861 participants, with 11.1% cases of mobility decline.
claims.poster_quote: This study investigates whether temporal trajectories of 12 routine biomarkers can identify patients in the preclinical phase of mobility decline, using the All of Us Research Program (N=297,861; 11.1% cases).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Using the All of Us Research Program (N = 297,861; 11.1% cases)...
claims.reason: Source: Abstract, third sentence. The dataset size and case percentage are explicitly stated.

claims.text: A hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL that declined from 13.5 over 3 years signals higher risk than one stable at 11.5 g/dL.
claims.poster_quote: A hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL that declined from 13.5 over 3 years signals higher risk than one stable at 11.5.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL that has been stable for three years represents a fundamentally different risk than one that declined from 13.5 g/dL over the same period.
claims.reason: Source: Introduction, paragraph 4. The paper explicitly discusses this example.

claims.text: Existing tools require structured assessments not embedded in primary care.
claims.poster_quote: Existing tools require structured assessments not embedded in primary care.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Existing frailty tools, such as the Fried phenotype, the Short Physical Performance Battery, and the Timed Up-and-Go, require structured functional assessments, manual scoring, or dedicated patient interaction not consistently embedded in primary care workflows.
claims.reason: Source: Introduction, paragraph 2. The paper confirms that existing tools require structured assessments not embedded in primary care.

claims.text: Trajectory features significantly outperformed static summaries in AUROC (0.797 vs. 0.755, DeLong p<0.001).
claims.poster_quote: Trajectory features significantly outperformed static summaries: AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755 (DeLong p<0.001).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: LightGBM models incorporating trajectories significantly outperformed static laboratory summaries (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755; DeLong p < 0.001).
claims.reason: Source: Abstract, fourth sentence. The AUROC improvement and significance are explicitly stated.

claims.text: Trajectory features significantly outperformed static summaries in AUPRC (0.380 vs. 0.304).
claims.poster_quote: Trajectory features significantly outperformed static summaries: AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755 (DeLong p<0.001); AUPRC 0.380 vs. 0.304.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Trajectory AUPRC was 0.380 versus 0.304 for baseline - a 25% relative improvement...
claims.reason: Source: Results, Trajectory Features Improve Discrimination, paragraph 2. The AUPRC improvement is explicitly stated.

claims.text: A 1:1 matched analysis confirmed independent trajectory signal with AUROC 0.727 vs. demographics-only 0.680.
claims.poster_quote: A 1:1 matched analysis confirmed independent trajectory signal (AUROC 0.727 vs. demographics-only 0.680).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A 1:1 age- and sex-matched analysis confirmed an independent trajectory signal (AUROC 0.727 vs. demographics-only 0.680).
claims.reason: Source: Abstract, fourth sentence. The matched analysis and AUROC values are explicitly stated.

claims.text: Prediction horizon analysis showed sustained discrimination 3–12 months before decline onset (AUROC 0.768–0.740).
claims.poster_quote: Prediction horizon analysis showed sustained discrimination 3–12 months before decline onset (AUROC 0.768–0.740).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A horizon analysis demonstrated sustained prediction 3–12 months before decline onset (AUROC 0.768–0.740).
claims.reason: Source: Abstract, fourth sentence. The prediction horizon analysis and AUROC range are explicitly stated.

claims.text: Top SHAP features include BMI mean (0.141), diastolic BP slope (0.104), and RDW mean (0.094).
claims.poster_quote: Top SHAP features: BMI mean (0.141), diastolic BP slope (0.104), RDW mean (0.094).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: By mean |SHAP| on 5,000 held-out observations, the top physiologic trajectory features were BMI mean (0.141), systolic blood pressure mean (0.113), diastolic blood pressure slope (0.104), RDW mean (0.094)...
claims.reason: Source: Results, Feature importance, paragraph 1. The SHAP feature rankings are explicitly stated.

claims.text: Count features ranked highest, such as sodium count (0.198), reflecting 'informative observation'.
claims.poster_quote: Count features ranked highest (e.g., sodium count: 0.198), reflecting ’informative observation’ — measurement frequency correlates with disease severity.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A distinctive finding is the high SHAP importance of measurement count features (sodium count: 0.198; BMI count: 0.189; RDW count: 0.161)...
claims.reason: Source: Results, Informative observation as confounder and signal, paragraph 1. The SHAP importance of count features is explicitly stated.

claims.text: Removing count features reduced AUROC only slightly (0.789), confirming model robustness.
claims.poster_quote: Removing count features reduced AUROC only slightly (0.789), confirming model robustness.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Removing count features yielded AUROC 0.789 (0.786–0.791), a reduction of 0.009 (DeLong p < 0.001).
claims.reason: Source: Results, Sensitivity analyses and calibration, paragraph 1. The slight AUROC reduction is explicitly stated.

claims.text: Isotonic calibration improved Brier score from 0.174 to 0.083 without degrading discrimination.
claims.poster_quote: Isotonic calibration improved Brier score from 0.174 to 0.083 without degrading discrimination.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Isotonic calibration reduced Brier score from 0.174 to 0.083 (52.3% improvement) without degrading discrimination (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.796).
claims.reason: Source: Results, Sensitivity analyses and calibration, paragraph 2. The calibration improvement is explicitly stated.

claims.text: At risk thresholds 0.20 and 0.25, NRI gains were 0.077 and 0.124, driven by improved specificity.
claims.poster_quote: At risk thresholds 0.20 and 0.25, NRI gains were 0.077 and 0.124, driven by improved specificity.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: At risk thresholds of 0.20 and 0.25, the trajectory model achieved NRI of 0.077 and 0.124 over baseline...
claims.reason: Source: Results, Sensitivity analyses and calibration, paragraph 2. The NRI gains are explicitly stated.

claims.text: The model achieves AUROC 0.797 using only 12 routine lab biomarkers.
claims.poster_quote: Our model achieves AUROC 0.797 using only 12 routine lab biomarkers — no diagnosis codes, medications, or functional assessments — making it a passive digital biomarker deployable in any EHR.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our model achieves AUROC 0.797 using only twelve laboratory biomarkers...
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, Trajectory features as passive digital biomarkers, paragraph 1. The AUROC and feature set are explicitly stated.

claims.text: The model does not use diagnosis codes, medications, or functional assessments.
claims.poster_quote: Our model achieves AUROC 0.797 using only 12 routine lab biomarkers — no diagnosis codes, medications, or functional assessments — making it a passive digital biomarker deployable in any EHR.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ...no diagnosis codes, medications, functional assessments, or free-text processing.
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, Trajectory features as passive digital biomarkers, paragraph 1. The exclusion of these features is explicitly stated.

claims.text: The 12-month detection horizon enables pre-clinical intervention.
claims.poster_quote: The 12-month detection horizon enables pre-clinical intervention.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The horizon analysis further demonstrates that these signals are detectable up to 12 months before diagnosis...
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, paragraph 1. The detection horizon is explicitly stated.

claims.text: BMI mean and diastolic BP slope are top predictors, aligning with known pathways: sarcopenia and autonomic dysregulation.
claims.poster_quote: BMI mean and diastolic BP slope are top predictors, aligning with known pathways: sarcopenia and autonomic dysregulation.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: BMI mean was the highest-ranked predictor (mean |SHAP| = 0.141)... Diastolic blood pressure slope, the leading trajectory-specific feature (0.104)...
claims.reason: Source: Results, Feature importance, paragraph 1. The predictors and their pathways are explicitly stated.

claims.text: RDW mean reflects systemic inflammation, independent of hemoglobin.
claims.poster_quote: RDW mean reflects systemic inflammation, independent of hemoglobin.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: RDW mean (0.094) is a notable finding: elevated RDW reflects erythropoietic instability driven by chronic inflammation...
claims.reason: Source: Results, Feature importance, paragraph 2. The systemic inflammation link is explicitly stated.

claims.text: AUPRC improvement (+0.076, 25%) matters more than AUROC improvement (+0.042, 6%) because it rewards precision.
claims.poster_quote: AUPRC improvement (+0.076, 25%) matters more than AUROC (+0.042, 6%) because it rewards precision — critical for reducing clinician alert fatigue.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The relative gain in AUPRC (+0.076, 25%) substantially exceeds the relative gain in AUROC (+0.042, 6%)...
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, Why AUPRC improvement matters more than AUROC improvement, paragraph 1. The relative improvements are explicitly stated.

claims.text: Informative observation (count features) is a confounder but not essential; model retains 99% discrimination without it.
claims.poster_quote: Informative observation (count features) is a confounder but not essential; model retains 99% discrimination without it, supporting equitable deployment in safety-net settings.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Removing count features yielded AUROC 0.789 (0.786–0.791), a reduction of 0.009...
claims.reason: Source: Results, Sensitivity analyses and calibration, paragraph 1. The confounder and retained discrimination are explicitly stated.

claims.text: ICD-10 outcomes may miss objective decline.
claims.poster_quote: Limitations: ICD-10 outcomes may miss objective decline; CRP and vitamin D have high missingness; no comorbidity adjustment.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ICD-10-coded outcomes capture documented recognition rather than objective functional performance...
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, Limitations, paragraph 1. The limitation of ICD-10 outcomes is explicitly stated.

claims.text: CRP and vitamin D have high missingness.
claims.poster_quote: Limitations: ICD-10 outcomes may miss objective decline; CRP and vitamin D have high missingness; no comorbidity adjustment.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: CRP and 25-hydroxyvitamin D contribute a limited trajectory signal due to selective ordering (82%–98% and 80%–88% missing, respectively)...
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, Limitations, paragraph 1. The high missingness is explicitly stated.

claims.text: No comorbidity adjustment was performed.
claims.poster_quote: Limitations: ICD-10 outcomes may miss objective decline; CRP and vitamin D have high missingness; no comorbidity adjustment.

claims.paper_evidence: Comorbidity adjustment was not performed.
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, Limitations, paragraph 1. The absence of comorbidity adjustment is explicitly stated.

claims.text: External validation and objective endpoints (e.g., gait speed) are needed.
claims.poster_quote: External validation and objective endpoints (e.g., gait speed) are needed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: External validation in independent health systems is required before deployment...
claims.reason: Source: Discussion, Limitations, paragraph 1. The need for external validation is explicitly stated.

claims.text: Participants aged 50–125 with EHR data and at least one lab measurement were selected.
claims.poster_quote: We used the All of Us Controlled Tier Dataset (v8), selecting participants aged 50–125 with EHR data and at least one lab measurement.

claims.paper_evidence: Eligible participants were aged 50-125 years with available EHR data and at least one recorded laboratory measurement.
claims.reason: Source: Methods, Dataset and Study Population, paragraph 1. The selection criteria are explicitly stated.

claims.text: Cases were defined by ICD-10 codes for mobility decline (e.g., R26.2, R26.9, W19).

claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Mobility decline cases were identified from the OMOP condition occurrence table using ICD-10-CM source concept identifiers: difficulty in walking (R26.2), unspecified gait and mobility abnormalities (R26.9)...

claims.text: Controls had no such codes; pseudo-index dates were randomly assigned within their lab window to avoid immortal time bias.

claims.text: Twelve biomarkers were selected a priori based on pathophysiologic links to functional decline.

claims.paper_evidence: Twelve biomarkers with established pathophysiologic links to functional decline were selected a priori...

claims.text: Trajectory features (slope, variability, delta, mean, count) were derived over a 3-year pre-index window.

claims.text: SHAP interpretability was computed on a held-out 20% test set.

claims.text: Longitudinal trajectory features from 12 routine biomarkers significantly outperform static summaries for predicting functional decline (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755; AUPRC 0.380 vs. 0.304; p<0.001).

claims.text: A matched analysis confirms independent trajectory signal (AUROC 0.727).

claims.text: Removing utilization-proxy features preserves 99% discrimination (AUROC 0.789).
